source.author: ov
source.text: Non ita fata sinunt, quoniam ieiunia virgo solverat et, cultis dum simplex errat in hortis, Poeniceum curva decerpserat arbore pomum sumptaque pallenti septem de cortice grana presserat ore suo.
source.text_original: Non ita fata sinunt, quoniam ieiunia virgo / solverat et, cultis dum simplex errat in hortis, / Poeniceum curva decerpserat arbore pomum / sumptaque pallenti septem de cortice grana / presserat ore suo.
source.text_english: The fates do not permit it, because the girl had broken her fast; and while, in her innocence, she wandered through the tended gardens, she had plucked a Punic apple from the bent tree and, taking seven seeds from its pale rind, had pressed them with her own mouth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quin etiam in thalamis primoque in limine Acasti fusus humo iuvenis gressus et inania signa ore premit sparsisque legens vestigia canis te quoque iam maesti forsan genitoris imago, nate, ait et luctus subeunt suspiria nostri, iamque dolos circumque trucis discrimina leti mille vides.
reuse.text_original: quin etiam in thalamis primoque in limine Acasti / fusus humo iuvenis gressus et inania signa / ore premit sparsisque legens vestigia canis / 'te quoque iam maesti forsan genitoris imago, / nate', ait 'et luctus subeunt suspiria nostri, / iamque dolos circumque trucis discrimina leti / mille vides.
reuse.text_english: Indeed, even in the chambers and on Acastus’ very threshold the young man, stretched out on the ground, presses with his face his steps and the empty traces, and, gathering up the scattered footprints, says: “You too, the image perhaps of your grieving father, my son, now come before my eyes, and the sighs of my sorrow come upon me; and now you see the thousand treacheries and, all around, the perils of cruel death.”
